evidence.quote: In the first quarter of Nvidia's fiscal year 2027, ending April 26, the company grew revenue 85% year over year, while diluted earnings per share soared by 140%.
evidence.one_line: Nvidia grew Q1 FY2027 revenue 85% year over year and diluted EPS 140% (author's retelling of company results).
evidence.speaker: Bram Berkowitz (fool.com)

evidence.quote: In March, CEO Jensen Huang said he expects the company's Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips to generate $1 trillion in sales between that time and the end of 2027.
evidence.one_line: CEO Jensen Huang said Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips should generate $1 trillion in sales from March 2026 through end-2027.
evidence.speaker: Jensen Huang (as reported by fool.com)

evidence.quote: Management said they think they can generate nearly $20 billion of CPU sales, making it an instant industry leader.
evidence.one_line: Nvidia management said it could generate nearly $20 billion of CPU sales after entering the CPU space.
evidence.speaker: Nvidia management (as reported by fool.com)

evidence.quote: Cerebras already has chips it claims are 15 times faster than some of Nvidia's models.
evidence.one_line: Cerebras claims its chips are 15 times faster than some Nvidia models.
evidence.speaker: Bram Berkowitz (fool.com), citing Cerebras claim

evidence.quote: Wall Street consensus estimates suggest the company will earn adjusted earnings per share of $8.97 in its current fiscal year.
evidence.one_line: Wall Street consensus expects Nvidia adjusted EPS of $8.97 in the current fiscal year (FY2027).
evidence.speaker: Bram Berkowitz (fool.com), citing Wall Street consensus

evidence.quote: Nvidia trading at roughly 22 times forward earnings
evidence.one_line: Nvidia trades at roughly 22 times forward earnings per the author.
evidence.speaker: Bram Berkowitz (fool.com)

evidence.quote: Nvidia has had an average forward price-to-earnings ratio of nearly 34 for the past two years.
evidence.one_line: Author states Nvidia's average forward P/E was nearly 34 over the past two years.
evidence.speaker: Bram Berkowitz (fool.com)
